Performers
Geraldine Farrar (Carmen, soprano), Walter B. Rogers (conductor), Orchestra, players not individually identified (orchestral accompaniment) Documented

The Library of Congress supplies the conductor for matrix B-15474, take 2. Its catalogued issue is Victor 621; FAU connects the same matrix and take to Victor 87210, the issue digitised here.

[1] [4] [3]
Work version
French-language solo recording of the Habanera, with orchestral accompaniment; both verses and the closing refrain Documented

A complete commercial aria side, not a recording of the surrounding stage scene. The English title on the disc describes the aria; the performance is in French. Ensemble participation in the stage score is not claimed for this solo recording.

[1] [3] [7]
Recorded
1914-12-09 Documented

Recording date, distinct from the February 1915 release bulletin and the 2021 Archive accession.

[4] [3]
Place
New York, United States Documented

No particular studio address is asserted.

[4]
Label
Victor / Victrola Documented

The digitised pressing is labelled Victrola; the contemporary release bulletin lists it under the Victor Talking Machine Company.

[1] [3] [5]
Catalogue
87210 Documented

Ten-inch, single-sided Red Seal issue, announced in the February 1915 list.

[1] [3] [5]
Matrix, take, sides
B-15474, take 2; single side Documented

IA transcribes an inscription as 3L87210. That inscription is retained as transfer metadata, not substituted for the recording matrix identified by FAU and the Library of Congress.

[3] [4]
Transfer
George Blood L.P.; digitisation and metadata: Nicholas Hoffman; cleaning: Kevin Coupe Documented

Credits reproduced from the Great 78 Project item metadata.

[1]
Transfer date
Unknown Unknown

The item became public on 19 October 2021. The exact digitisation date is not established and is not replaced by that upload date.

[1]
Processing
Four stylus transfers were made; the selected friendly-filename transfer was preferred by the digitising engineer. Flat and equalised versions are described, with 500 Hz turnover for the latter. Documented

The notes name 3.8, 2.3, 2.8 and 3.3 mil truncated-conical styli but do not unambiguously identify the chosen stylus or equalisation for the friendly-filename MP3. Surface noise, distortion and small pops are noted by the archive; no site-side restoration is added.

[1] [2]
Composition rights
Public domain: Bizet’s 1875 score and the nineteenth-century French text Documented

Bizet died in 1875; the Habanera’s text is his own. This is the original French aria, not a modern translation or arrangement.

[6] [7]
Recording rights
Public domain in the United States: commercially published in 1915, before the 1923 statutory boundary Documented

The Talking Machine World, January 1915, p. 62, lists Victor 87210 under ‘The February Red Seal Records’. This establishes publication independently of the December 1914 session and the Archive’s generic 1914 date. Under the Classics Protection and Access Act, protection for pre-1923 publications ended on 31 December 2021. No worldwide-rights claim is made.

[5] [8]
